items.name: syncrobotic-theme
items.title: SYNCROBOTIC theme
items.description: Colour, radius, type, height and motion tokens. Replaces the :root, .dark and @theme blocks from shadcn init.

changelog.note: `--chart-1-foreground` … `--chart-5-foreground` (utilities `text-chart-N-foreground`): ink for words and numbers on a chart colour, 4.5:1 or more on it in light, dark and both high-contrast modes. `--color-scrim` (`bg-scrim`) and a new `--letterbox` (`bg-letterbox`) for the bars around a picture: the dark page colour, black in high contrast. Issue #302. New `--thumb` (`bg-thumb`): the knob you drag on a slider and a switch that is off; white in every mode, as before, but a theme can now change it. Issue #301.
Dark theme: `--annotate-predicted` is the high-contrast indigo (#b5b4ff), so a predicted box keeps 3:1 against the photo around it, not only against its halo.
High contrast defines --stop and --stop-deep: white on the stop reaches 7:1 (it was 4.8:1), on the deep red 13.7:1.

A field the browser autofills keeps the theme's background and text colour (Chrome painted it light blue, also in dark mode). The page tells the browser its colour scheme (light, dark inside .dark), so native scrollbars, pickers and autofill follow the theme.
New `no-data` utility: a hatch and inset outline in the field-edge colour (3:1), for a chart cell or bar with no value, so missing data never passes for zero.
Chart greys re-stepped so Other (`--chart-4`) is 3:1 on a card in every mode, like the other series, and every pair still differs by ΔE 15 (also to colour-blind eyes).

New chart palette, graphite and one accent: --chart-1 is the brand indigo (#5347a8 in light) for the series the reader should look at, --chart-2 and --chart-3 graphite steps for the others, --chart-4 a light grey for Other, --chart-5 the baseline (an alias of --chart-3). Derived for dark and both high-contrast modes, and checked against each card: any two of slots 1–3, and 3 beside 4, differ by ΔE 15 or more to normal vision and under red-green colour blindness; slots 1–3 reach 3:1. The names are unchanged; their meaning is not, so a chart that used slots 2–5 as hues now draws them grey.

New --track (tracks and quiet shapes, 1.5:1 on card, page and popover) and --shadow-selected; --disabled raised to 3:1 on every surface in every mode; dark --popover one step above the card so overlays separate.

Comments only: the header states one rule per topic (light is the default; a running piece of work is blue, its state word grey; waiting loops only) and points to the Motion and Colour foundations instead of repeating them. No token changed.

--input (the edge of fields, checkboxes, radios and a switch that is off) is now 3:1 on the card, the page and a muted tile (WCAG 1.4.11): #80808a light, #72727a dark. It was 1.2–1.4:1, and on a card that edge is all that shows where a control is. The header says light is :root and dark the .dark class, and that offline is a neutral state.

Annotation tokens for boxes and points on images: `--annotate-predicted` (chart-1), `--annotate-truth` (chart-2), `--annotate-previous` (muted ink), `--annotate-selected` (focus ink) and `--annotate-halo` (white in light, black in dark, at least 3:1 under every stroke), plus `--annotate-fade` (0.6; 1 in high contrast), as `stroke-annotate-*` utilities.

A search field in an input group with a button in it no longer shows the browser's clear cross as well: one cross, not two. `--disabled` is 3:1 on the page and cards (#84848c light, #6e6e76 dark), still lighter than secondary text. Fieldsets can shrink (min-width 0), so fields inside never push past a phone's edge.
Sheet animations travel the extra 8 px (and the home indicator) of the floating sheet.

High contrast: `data-contrast="more"` on `<html>` or a container, in light or dark, for bright sun and low vision. Text and status reach 7:1 on every surface, edges 3:1, trays over the map turn opaque. Fixed: a `.dark` subtree on a light page kept light-mode ink on cards, menus and secondary buttons.
A search field's clear button is the kit's grey cross at 20 px instead of the browser's small blue one.
Touch is detected with `any-pointer: coarse`, so a touch laptop with a trackpad keeps 44 px controls, and compact density applies only where nothing is a touch screen.
`--h-thumb` (the slide-to-release thumb: the stop less its inset), so the thumb fills the track in glove and compact density.

Density: `data-density="glove"` (48 px controls, 64 px rows and stop) and `data-density="compact"` (36 px controls, 40 px rows, mouse only; touch keeps 44) on `<html>` or any container. The stop never shrinks.

Focus ring is the foreground colour, no longer the in-progress blue. Chart palette moves off the status hues (violet, teal, olive, magenta, grey for Other), CVD-validated. Type scale gains 2xl (24, figures) and 4xl (36, hero on phones) and is locked: sizes off the scale produce nothing. Adds radius-2xs (4) for controls 24 px and smaller. Warning and danger are told apart by hue and lightness (deutan ΔE 10.8 light / 21.6 dark, was 1.5; 4.8:1 or more as text on every surface). Adds --ease-exit for exits. Blue is defined: a process someone is waiting on, never a state. Adds animate-route-progress (off under reduced motion).
caret-blink animation for one-time-code boxes; stops under reduced motion.
The focus ring appears in the ring colour at once (outline colour set before focus; transition-colors used to fade it from the text colour).
Compact density is for a mouse only: on touch (pointer: coarse) --h-sm is 44 px. The spinner stops under reduced motion. Selected-state rule written down.

Calmer status hues in both modes (all still ≥ 4.5:1 on every surface); colour rule: colour is for what is abnormal. Motion tokens as CSS: appear/disappear, fade-in, sheet-in/out per side, expand/collapse, and the press utility. Chart series tokens --chart-1…5 for light and dark, validated for colour-vision deficiency.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: feedback

items.name: labels-zh-tw
items.title: Labels: Traditional Chinese (Taiwan)
items.description: The kit's words in Traditional Chinese as written in Taiwan: one typed labels object per component that takes `labels` (alarms, emergency stop, teleoperation, robot map and model, data grid, filters, forms and more), with numbers and units formatted by functions as in the English defaults.

changelog.note: `paginationLabels.range` groups its numbers by the locale ("第 1,201–1,220 筆，共 12,400 筆"), as the English default does. Issue #324. `notFoundPageLabels`, `noAccessPageLabels`, `errorPageLabels`, `offlinePageLabels` and `loadingPageLabels` for status-pages. Issue #323. `shellSearchLabels`. Issue #331.

`chipGroupLabels.selected`. `meterLabels`. `tierBadgeLabels` for the new tier-badge (可商用, 非商用, 受限, 僅限地端). `streamingTextLabels` for the new streaming-text. `groundedTextLabels` for the new grounded-text (圖上 8 個點, 文字中：8 隻斑馬). `topBarShellLabels`, and `paginationLabels.nav` (分頁). Issue #293.

`waypointEditorLabels` for the new waypoint-editor. `cameraWallLabels` for the new camera-wall. New geoMapLabels (and geoMapListLabels) for the new geo-map: fixes (RTK 固定解, 未定位), coordinates as 北緯 / 東經, headings with the compass point, and the goal card. New `attitudeIndicatorLabels` and `gaugeLabels` for the new attitude item.

New streamingChartLabels, diagnosticsLabels for the new streaming-chart and diagnostics, sidebarProviderLabels for the new sidebar, logViewerLabels for the new log-viewer, and `details` in `treeLabels`. dataGridLabels has width, wider, narrower, resetWidth and cannotSelect for the data grid's new resize and selection words. Adds `batteryUnknown` to islandLabels and `viewOptions` to streamingChartLabels; the Bluetooth-only stop says 藍牙 and the map's retry says 重新載入.
First release.

items.name: ros
items.title: ROS
items.description: ROS and ROS 2 over rosbridge with no ROS library: a rosbridge v2 client on the browser's WebSocket (ref-counted subscriptions and advertisements, capped jittered reconnect that resubscribes, a send queue, service calls with a timeout, a zero Twist when a velocity publisher stops or the link drops) and pure converters from OccupancyGrid, LaserScan, PointCloud2, JointState, NavSatFix and GeoPoint, Imu and Odometry, DiagnosticArray, /rosout Log and poses to the kit's components, a web_video_server URL for an image topic, and from a teleop command, a map goal and a waypoint route back to Twist, PoseStamped, nav_msgs/Path and Nav2's NavigateThroughPoses goal (and the route back from them).

changelog.note: `detection2DArrayToAnnotations` turns a `vision_msgs/Detection2DArray` (ROS 2 Humble on, or the older layout) into annotated-image's boxes, labelled with each detection's best class (through `classes`) and score, for annotated-image and the marks grounded-text's spans point at.

`waypointsToPath` and `waypointsToNavigateThroughPoses` turn waypoint-editor's route into a `nav_msgs/Path` and the goal of Nav2's NavigateThroughPoses (PoseStamped in the map frame; a waypoint without a heading faces the next one), and `pathToWaypoints` and `navigateThroughPosesToWaypoints` turn them back (Kilted's `nav_msgs/Goals` too). `webVideoServerSrc(server, topic, { quality })` builds the web_video_server URL a `<video>` plays for a `sensor_msgs/Image` topic (VP8 WebM by default, H.264 for Safari), sized by camera-wall's quality hint (`webVideoQuality`: low 640×360, high 1280×720). `navSatFixToGeo` turns a `sensor_msgs/NavSatFix` into geo-map's robot fields (`lat`, `lon`, the fix in words from the status and covariance, and the horizontal accuracy in metres); `geoPointToGeo` reads a `geographic_msgs/GeoPoint`, GeoPose or GeoPoseStamped; `geoGoalToGeoPoseStamped` and `geoGoalToNavSatFix` send a geo-map goal back; `enuYawToHeading` and `headingToEnuYaw` convert between ENU yaw and compass headings. `imuToAttitude` turns a `sensor_msgs/Imu` into roll and pitch in degrees (REP 103 signs) and a compass heading (ENU, REP 145; `{ heading: false }` for an IMU without a magnetometer), for attitude's AttitudeIndicator; `quaternionToEuler` gives roll, pitch and yaw as tf2's getRPY does; `odometryToSpeed` turns `nav_msgs/Odometry` (or a Twist) into a speed in m/s for attitude's Gauge.

`diagnosticArrayToStatuses` turns a `diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray` into diagnostics' `statuses` (the level byte read however the bridge wrote it, each status stamped `receivedAt`), and `mergeDiagnostics` keeps the latest status of each name as /diagnostics arrives a few at a time; `rosLogToLogLine` turns a /rosout message (ROS 2 `rcl_interfaces/msg/Log` or ROS 1 `rosgraph_msgs/Log`) into log-viewer's LogLine: the stamp in ms, the level as a word, the node as the source, and the file, function and line.
First release.

items.name: use-long-press
items.title: useLongPress
items.description: Press and hold with progress from 0 to 1.

changelog.note: The frame loop is declared inside the press handler instead of referring to itself before its declaration, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: use-slide-release
items.title: useSlideRelease
items.description: Drag, threshold and spring-back logic for slide to release.

changelog.note: Safety: a keyboard hold is cancelled when focus leaves the track or the page is hidden (a held Enter followed by Tab used to release 2 s later anyway). The thumb travels while the key is held, so the keyboard shows its progress, and aria-valuenow with it.
`reset` is stable, so an effect can depend on it.
The release pulse comes from `feedback` (`release`), so an app can turn touch off in one place.
Fix: the thumb follows the finger 1:1. It used to speed up mid-drag and finish on its own.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: use-presence
items.title: usePresence
items.description: Keeps an element, or list items, on screen while they leave, so exits use the disappear movement instead of vanishing.

changelog.note: Showing again mounts in the same render instead of an effect later, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
First release.

items.name: use-debounce
items.title: useDebounce
items.description: A value, or a function call, that waits until changes pause: a search sent when the typing stops, not on every key.

changelog.note: useDebouncedCallback keeps its timer and pending arguments in a closure instead of refs read during render, so it is safe under the React Compiler. Same behaviour: one stable function per delay, always calling the latest fn.
First release: useDebouncedValue and useDebouncedCallback (with cancel and flush).

items.name: use-ros
items.title: useRos
items.description: React hooks over the ros client: RosProvider, useRosStatus, useRosTopic (the latest message, through useSyncExternalStore), useRosPublisher (a stable publish function; a zero Twist on unmount, hidden page and dropped link for cmd_vel) and useRosService (a call with a timeout).

changelog.note: First release.

items.name: use-hotkeys
items.title: useHotkeys
items.description: Keyboard shortcuts as a map of keys to handlers ({ "1": yes, "mod+z": undo, "?": help }), quiet while someone types in a field, with the key being pressed for Kbd.

changelog.note: First release: useHotkeys(map, { enabled }) with mod/ctrl/meta/alt/shift combos, keys ignored in text fields unless allowInInput, no repeats unless asked, and `pressed` for <Kbd pressed>.

items.name: status-glyph
items.title: Status glyph
items.description: Status as a shape, coloured only when abnormal: filled circle busy, hollow circle normal, triangle attention, square stopped, slashed circle offline (grey).

changelog.note: Docs: the glyph is hidden from screen readers (say the status in words), active is "busy" everywhere, and offline is grey, never coloured; `tone` is marked deprecated in its props.
No unused React import, so the file compiles in projects with noUnusedLocals.

`status` (active, normal, warning, danger, offline) replaces `tone`, whose info, success and neutral named colours for states that are not coloured. `tone` still works until 1.0 and warns once in development. New `Status`, `toStatus`, `statusText`, `statusSubtle`.
`toneSubtle` tints only warning and danger; busy (info) and normal (success) are grey, like their text. A calm notice on the island no longer turns blue or green.
Docs: the filled circle is an active (busy) state, drawn in ink.
In progress and normal use the text colour; only warning, danger and offline are coloured.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: status-eyebrow
items.title: Status eyebrow
items.description: The state word above a headline, and the same status inside a list row.

changelog.note: StatusEyebrow and InlineStatus take `status`; `tone` still works until 1.0.
Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: tray
items.title: Tray
items.description: The shared frame of the dynamic island and the dock: radius 24, padding 8, gap 8.

changelog.note: First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: stop-button
items.title: Emergency stop
items.description: One touch stops; hold 2 s to stop all; lying down it becomes wake and stand up. UI only: sending and the Bluetooth fallback live in the app.

changelog.note: The hold-to-stop-all fill is opaque --stop-deep, so the label keeps its contrast over it (it was white at 20 %, 3.8:1). The label no longer moves when “Keep holding” takes over. Bluetooth only says so in words (“Emergency stop · Bluetooth”). The tag shows on the deep red of a stop delivered over Bluetooth.
WakeButton's disabled reason is 14 px (it was 12 px and dim).
“No connection” and WakeButton's disabled reason are readable (muted text on muted, not white on grey or the disabled colour, which measured 2.1–2.6:1).
Buzzes: one pulse at the touch, two when the robot confirms, two long ones when it does not (the `feedback` patterns).
Imports CircleAlert by its current Lucide name (AlertCircle was an alias); no visual change.
Presses.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: slide-to-release
items.title: Slide to release
items.description: Past 85% releases, short of that springs back in 200 ms; locked for viewers; hold 2 s on the keyboard instead.

changelog.note: Safety: a keyboard hold is cancelled on blur and when the page is hidden. The thumb travels while Enter or Space is held; `keyboardHint` (read after the label) tells a screen reader to hold; `releasing` shows the released state without a slide. The fill, the tag and the locked thumb are opaque (high contrast allows nothing translucent).

`failed` and `failedLabel`: when the robot does not release, the thumb goes back and the label says to slide again, instead of staying on Releasing…. The thumb follows `--h-thumb`, so it fills the track in every density.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: teleop-pad
items.title: Teleop pad
items.description: Drive a mobile robot by hand with a dead-man stick: it moves only while held and stops the moment input is let go or lost. Fixed-rate commands, dead zone, speed cap, keyboard.

changelog.note: Disabled, its description says why and no longer reads out the drive keys.
The latest stop is swapped in after each commit instead of during render, and the pointer-end handlers are no longer built in render, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.

First release: a dead-man stick (pointer: touch, mouse, pen) sending { linear, angular } at rateHz while held, zero and onStop with the reason on release, pointer cancel, blur, hidden page or timeoutMs; dead zone, maxSpeed shown as a scale, keyboard drive with arrows or W A S D and Space to stop, status with icon and words, glove density, reduced motion, haptic ticks. `timeoutMs={false}` turns the pointer timeout off, for robots that run their own watchdog.

items.name: dock
items.title: Dock
items.description: Three tiers: state action, this page's primary action, navigation.

changelog.note: The tab count uses CountBadge. Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component. Tabs put the label under the icon below 384 px of dock, so four tabs fit a 360 px phone; action labels wrap instead of running past the edge.
The destructive action is a danger outline, not a tinted fill.
Buttons press.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: island
items.title: Dynamic island
items.description: Name, device status and notifications, each zone expanding on its own; notices and the most urgent unacknowledged alarm live inside the island.

changelog.note: `battery` has no default: without a reading the island says the level is unknown (“–%”, “battery unknown”) instead of showing 72 %. A robot without a picture gets a square avatar with its initials, not an empty circle. The bell is a 44 px square target (it was 36 px wide). New label `batteryUnknown`.
The leaving notice and the last alarm are kept in state set during render instead of refs written during render, so they are safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
IslandAlarm follows the alarm redesign: never tinted (the edge, glyph and priority word carry the colour), the time first in tabular figures, a lighter Acknowledge.
Tracks and quiet shapes use the new --track token, so they read in dark mode (1.5:1 on their surface; they were near invisible).
In high contrast the action buttons are opaque with an --input edge. A · in the title holds to the word after it.
The battery turns warning below 15 %, the fleet-wide threshold (it was 30 %). Offline is documented as neutral.
Alarm and notice text wraps to two lines instead of being cut, and the buttons move to their own row when space is short.
Island takes `status` for the robot's state; `tone` still works until 1.0. The docs pair the edge as `alarmEdge(topAlarm(alarms)) ?? stateEdge`, so a low alarm does not erase offline or stopped.
The status button says offline and charging (new `offline`, `charging`, `battery` labels), not only a low battery.

IslandAlarm buzzes, sounds and announces new alarms like AlarmList (on a phone it is the alarm surface), and keeps its live regions mounted when empty. “+N more” counts only live alarms. `feedback={false}` when an AlarmList on the same screen already signals.
The unread count uses CountBadge. Notices and the island alarm leave with disappear. Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
Buttons are rounded-xs and 14 px text; the unread count uses the danger tint like the dock.
IslandAlarm tints only critical alarms; Acknowledge is an outline button. Notices and the alarm appear; zones and buttons press.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: list
items.title: Grouped list
items.description: One surface with inset dividers; icons only when they carry meaning; status as shape plus word.

changelog.note: The lead icon sits on the title's line, not the middle of title and meta.
Only pressable rows press.
Rows press.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: What is known shows first; only unknown values get a skeleton; the whole group breathes.

changelog.note: Tracks and quiet shapes use the new --track token, so they read in dark mode (1.5:1 on their surface; they were near invisible). Bone onCard is deprecated (no effect).
Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
LoadingLine uses the Spinner (its delay and track).
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Primary, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive and link; 36, 44 and 48 px; loading state with a delayed spinner.

changelog.note: Disabled outline and destructive buttons keep their outline and lose the ink (--disabled text, border ring). They were a filled grey, which looked heavier than the enabled outline beside them, as in pagination.

Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight. A loading button keeps its look (busy is not unavailable) and still blocks a second press.
The link variant is foreground with an underline (was blue): a link reads by its underline; blue means in progress.
Small buttons carry 16 px icons.
Presses (scale 0.97 at --motion-fast).
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: geo-map
items.title: Geo map
items.description: An outdoor map in latitude and longitude for robots that work outside (patrol, agriculture, delivery), drawn in SVG with no map library: Web Mercator raster tiles from your own tile server ({z}/{x}/{y}) with their attribution, or a coordinate grid that needs no network; robots as status shapes with heading, an accuracy circle and their GPS fix in words; geofences (keep-outs hatched), a route with numbered waypoints and trails; pan and zoom by drag, wheel, pinch, buttons and keys, a scale bar in m and km; a goal placed by pointer or keys and sent on confirm; GeoMapList shows the same robots as text.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `geo-map-list-item`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
Each robot's name label has a `key`, so a product on eslint-config-next (react/jsx-key) gets no error from the unmodified file. Issue #301.
First release.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: Appears only after 300 ms, so quick work never flashes a spinner.

changelog.note: Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels.loading`; `label` still works and wins.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented control
items.description: Switch between views of the same data. The selected segment is inverted.

changelog.note: value, defaultValue and onValueChange are its own documented props (one segment always stays selected); behaviour unchanged.
One segment always stays selected: pressing the selected one again no longer clears the choice (it called onValueChange("")).
In high contrast the track has an --input edge (3:1). The thumb re-measures when a segment resizes, so it never drifts off the selected segment.
The selected thumb travels to the segment you pick (Move pattern, --motion-base); the label colour changes with it.
Each segment's hit area reaches the track's edges, so a finger gets 44 px though the segment draws 36.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
Presses.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: An on/off button for a layer or option. On is inverted, like a selected segment.

changelog.note: Disabled and on reads as disabled: a grey fill (muted-foreground) instead of the inverted one, like a disabled checked switch.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
First release. Presses.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy button
items.description: Copies a value; the icon becomes a check for 1.5 s.

changelog.note: A text button keeps its width when its word changes to Copied or Not copied (all three share one cell), and its name is the shown word once, not "Copied Copied": the announcement now sits beside the button.

Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`copy`, `copied`, `failed`, `notCopied`, which was fixed English). `label`, `copiedLabel` and `failedLabel` still work and win.

Works over plain HTTP (falls back to execCommand when the Clipboard API is missing or refused), says so when the copy fails instead of failing silently, and announces the result for icon buttons too. Exports copyText().
First release.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code block
items.description: Code or a command with a copy button: wraps a command between words, scrolls source sideways, hides a one-time secret until shown. Takes a highlighter's output as children.

changelog.note: labels.copy(title) names the copy button, so it can be translated; copyLabel still sets it as is.

First release: a framed block with a title and CopyButton; wrap="words" for shell commands, wrap="none" scrolls with the table's fade and takes focus; secret hides a one-time value behind Show; optional line numbers; a highlighter's output (shiki) as children.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: 44 px text field with 16 px text so iOS does not zoom; aria-invalid turns the edge danger.

changelog.note: Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface).
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
Error edge is 2 px, transitions at --motion-fast; no shake.
Focus ring transitions.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input group
items.description: An input with an icon, a unit or a button (clear, show password) inside its edge. The group draws the field, focus and error.

changelog.note: Wiring the Field's id onto the first text box no longer reassigns a variable from a callback, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface).
InputGroupUnit: a unit written right after the value ("120 m"), the value as wide as its text, instead of a unit at the far edge. A press on the field's empty space puts the caret in the text box.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
Disabled is a muted surface instead of 50 % opacity, so its text (a unit, a prefix) keeps readable contrast.
First release.

items.name: number-field
items.title: Number field
items.description: A number with a range, a step and a unit. Type freely, kept in range on blur; 44 px buttons; arrow keys, Shift, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End.

items.name: alarm
items.title: Alarm
items.description: ISA-18.2 alarms: three priorities with their own shape, colour and words, acknowledge and clear states, and a sorted list that announces new alarms to screen readers.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `alarm-action`, `alarm-shelve`, `alarm-unshelve`, `alarm-acknowledge`, `alarm-acknowledge-all`, `alarm-retry`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
Buttons beside Acknowledge (a custom action, Shelve) are ghost, so Acknowledge is the only outlined button in an unacknowledged row. Unshelve, alone in its row, keeps its outline.

"Acknowledge all" appears only when `onAcknowledgeAll` is passed (no longer from `onAcknowledge` alone), and never takes a critical alarm: each is acknowledged on its own row, and while one is unacknowledged the button reads "Acknowledge 3 non-critical" (label `acknowledgeNonCritical`).

Low priority is a diamond (`DiamondAlert`), not a circle: at 20 px the circle read as the critical octagon. AlarmList takes `status` ("loading" shows placeholder rows and never "No active alarms"; "error" says the list could not load or update, keeps what it has, with `onRetry` and `updatedAt`). Labels `loading`, `errorEmpty`, `errorStale`, `updatedAt`, `retry`. `useAlarmSignals` takes `ready`: alarms that arrive with the first load do not buzz.

Redesign: one list of aligned rows (glyph, time, priority and title, state and actions). Colour only on the glyph and the priority word, no tinted rows; unacknowledged is a bold title and a solid bar, cleared-not-acknowledged a dashed bar, acknowledged regular and grey with `acknowledgedAt`. Lighter Acknowledge, `onAcknowledgeAll` in the header, focus moves to the next Acknowledge. New: `acknowledgedAt`, `clearedAt`, `onAcknowledgeAll`, labels `clearedWhen`, `acknowledgeAll`, `acknowledgeShown`, `acknowledgedCount`.
A short last word stays joined to the one before it, so no lone "3" or "B" on a line.
A · in the meta line holds to the word after it, so it never dangles at a line end.
The priority icon sits on the title's first line instead of the middle of the block.

Signals follow the live list: shelved, suppressed and out-of-service alarms stay silent, an alarm back from shelving sounds again, and an unacknowledged critical alarm sounds every 10 s until acknowledged (as the Alarms foundation promised). Critical alarms are never shelved, whatever the data says. The flood clock moves on, so a flood ends when its alarms age out, and only live alarms count. In a flood screen readers hear one count. New `useAlarmSignals` and `AlarmAnnouncer` share all this with the island.

AlarmList buzzes and sounds for a new critical or high alarm (`feedback`, on by default; `feedback={false}` for a record view). The ISA-18.2 states beyond acknowledge: shelved (`shelvedUntil`, `onShelve`/`onUnshelve`; never critical), suppressed by design and out of service (counted under the list), and floods (over 10 in 10 minutes from `raisedAt`: a banner, low alarms folded, one announcement).
A cleared alarm fades out (disappear) instead of vanishing. Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
Buttons are rounded-xs, concentric with the card.
Only critical unacknowledged alarms are tinted; others are a bar and the word. Acknowledge is an outline button. New alarms appear; buttons press.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Transient feedback on what the user just did: 4 s, 8 s with an action, failures until dismissed. Call toast() anywhere; mount <Toaster /> once.

changelog.note: Escape inside an open native `<dialog>` closes the dialog (it gets a `cancel` it can refuse) and the toast stays; the toast had taken the key. Escape with focus in a toast, or outside any dialog, still dismisses it. Issue #311.

After a toast is dismissed with the pointer, the stack collapses and the timers run again once the pointer leaves (focus a click brought no longer holds them). On a phone the stack is full width with even 16 px gutters.

Toaster stacks toasts like sonner: newest in front, two more peeking behind it, the rest kept hidden (none is closed to make room) and brought forward as the front ones go; hover, focus or touch spreads the stack. Toasts arrive from the edge and the others move on transform, so a 4th no longer makes the stack jump. Only the first mounted Toaster draws (a second one drew every toast twice and paused only one copy); a swiped toast leaves from where it was let go. Toast wraps its icon and text in a [data-slot=toast-content] div.
Every toast uses the 16 px radius.
A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules.
Failures are never closed for you: when more than three toasts are open, the oldest that is not a failure makes room, and if all are failures, they all stay.
A failed toast uses CircleAlert, the kit's one icon for failed.
Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.

items.title: Sidebar
items.description: The main navigation of a console: a column of grouped links with counts, tags and nested pages, a header for a workspace or robot switcher and a footer for the account. Collapses to a rail of icons with tooltips (⌘B / Ctrl+B, kept in a cookie) and is a sheet on phones.

changelog.note: SidebarTrigger `show`: "expanded" renders only while the column is open on a wide screen (collapse, for SidebarHeader), "collapsed" only while it is a rail or hidden and always on phones (expand, and the menu that opens the sheet, for the top bar); "always" (default) is the single trigger as before. Pressed from the keyboard, the trigger that hides moves focus to the one that shows. New SidebarRail: the sidebar's edge as a mouse control (resize cursor, hairline on hover, the trigger's tooltip, a click toggles), aria-hidden and out of the Tab order, absent on touch and phones. The Sidebar's inner frame now clips the column instead of the aside, so the rail can reach over the edge; same look.

First release, in shadcn/ui's composition (SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarMenuSub, SidebarFooter, SidebarTrigger, useSidebar). A 240 px column that collapses to a 72 px rail of icons with tooltips, or off canvas; a sheet from the edge on phones. ⌘B / Ctrl+B toggles it and a cookie keeps the choice. The current page has the kit's muted fill and weight, counts are CountBadges (a dot on the rail), tags are quiet grey words, rows are 44 px and focus rings sit inside them.

items.name: graph
items.title: Graph
items.description: A directed acyclic graph for lineage and pipelines, laid out in layers with no layout library: boxes with name, meta, status and link, neutral edges, the selected node's path highlighted, arrow keys along the edges, and GraphList, the same graph as text.

changelog.note: Its controls carry a data-slot: `graph-node`, `graph-list-link`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
The path walk is written as plain statements instead of a comma expression. No visible change.

First release: a layered layout for up to about 60 nodes (longest-path layers, barycenter ordering, edges routed between boxes), left to right or top to bottom, scrolling inside its frame with the scroll fade; one Tab stop with arrow keys along the edges; selection highlights the upstream and downstream path; each node's name lists its inputs and outputs; GraphList shows the same graph as text.

items.name: robot-map
items.title: Robot map
items.description: A site floor plan in metres, drawn in SVG with no map library: a ROS occupancy grid and costmap as the floor, laser scans, zones as outlines with icon and name, planned and travelled routes, robots as status shapes with heading and name, selection, pan and zoom by drag, wheel, pinch, buttons and keys, a scale bar and an optional north arrow; goal, waypoint and zone editing by pointer and keys; RobotMapList shows the same robots as text.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `robot-map-list-item`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

Waypoints a list beside the map can drive: `selectedWaypoint` and `onWaypointSelect` select a waypoint from either side (and, given, a click selects one in view mode too); `onWaypointEdit` says which waypoint was added, moved or removed, by index; `waypointMarks` draws a waypoint's heading tick and the warning shape for a problem. In an edit mode the plan now fits below the mode banner, which covered points along its top edge.
The error shows the alert glyph above its words, as the point cloud and robot model do, and the retry button says “Load again”.

Fixes for live data and editing. A plan whose size arrives after the first render (a `grid` loaded later) is fitted again, unless someone has already panned or zoomed. A cancelled drag of a waypoint or zone corner (Esc, a second finger, pointercancel) sends the original back through onWaypointsChange / onZonesChange and says "Move cancelled". The selected or carried waypoint is followed by its value, so when the app changes the list (drops waypoint 1 as the robot reaches it) Delete and Esc act on that waypoint, or on none if it is gone. A fast costmap now shows: one encode at a time, the one in flight finishes and only updates between are skipped. With a floorplan the costmap is drawn over it. The keyboard crosshair's position (and a turning goal's heading) is announced once the arrows rest for 400 ms. Smaller: snap at a plan edge off the snap grid stays on the grid, the crosshair is drawn snapped where Enter places it, a new mode starts the crosshair at the centre, Enter during a pointer press sets the goal once, and a removed grid frees its image at once. Public API unchanged.

Layers from ROS and editing. `grid` draws a nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid as the floor (free the map surface, occupied a muted grey at its probability, unknown the no-data hatch), rasterised once per new data array; with no width and height the grid is the plan. `costmap` lays the accent's ramp over it with a legend in words. `scans` draws sensor_msgs/LaserScans as small neutral dots from each robot's pose, one path per scan, skipping invalid readings. `mode` (view, goal, waypoints, zone) places a goal and points it, adds, moves and removes numbered waypoints (grey, blue only with waypointsPlanned) and draws zones corner by corner (`editableZones` drags existing corners), all controlled, with optional `snap`. The primary pointer edits and the right or middle button or two fingers pan; a keyboard crosshair, Enter, Esc and Delete do the same, a banner says what a click does, and each edit is announced. New helpers `gridToPlan`, `rosToPlan`, `rasteriseGrid` and `scanToPoints`.
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
The frame size and scale refs are updated after each commit instead of during render, and gliding to a selected robot is an effect event, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.

First release: the site map that lived only inside map-workspace, as a component. Site coordinates in metres over an image or SVG floor plan; zones (no entry, slow, charging, other) as hairline outlines with icon and name; planned routes dashed blue, travelled tracks solid grey; robots as their status shape with a heading tick and a name that moves aside instead of covering another; selection by a ring and weight. Pan and zoom by drag, wheel (once focused, or with Ctrl), pinch, 44 px buttons and keys (arrows, + / -, 0), gliding at --motion-base unless motion is reduced. One Tab stop; RobotMapList lists the robots with position, zone and status, and selects on the map. Scale bar, optional north arrow, empty, loading and error states.

items.name: waypoint-editor
items.title: Waypoint editor
items.description: Plan a robot's route as an ordered list of waypoints, edited in a list and on robot-map together: each waypoint a name, a place in metres (or latitude and longitude), an optional heading, an action on arrival (wait, dock, take a photo, custom) and a dwell time. Reorder by drag or keys, add by clicking the map or a button, delete with Undo, duplicate; a row and its point select each other. Problems (outside the map, in a keep-out zone, too close, no name) show inline and Save says why it is disabled. Distance and estimated time, unsaved changes with Save and Cancel, a read-only mode, list first on a phone with the map a tab.

changelog.note: First release.

items.name: dialog

Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: DialogContent takes `labels.close`; `closeLabel` still works and wins.
The close button sits 8 px from the corner (concentric) and presses.
Scrim fades in; the dialog appears and disappears.

items.name: alert-dialog
items.title: Alert dialog

changelog.note: Its controls carry a data-slot: `alert-dialog-trigger`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #329.
Scrim fades in; the dialog appears and disappears.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet

SheetFooter pins to the sheet's bottom edge, so it no longer covers the last field and its focus ring.
SheetFooter sticks to the bottom with its own padding, so the main action is never cut.

Floats 8 px from the screen's edges, the app shell's gutter, with every corner rounded; the bottom sheet clears the home indicator. A side sheet fills up to max-w-sm with auto margins, so drop `w-full` from your SheetContent if you set it.
Titles are the sheet size (xl); the scrim leaves with the panel.
side="left" for navigation drawers. Slides in and out from its edge at --motion-sheet; scrim fades.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover

A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules.
Appears and disappears.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover card
items.description: A preview of what a link leads to, on hover and keyboard focus. Preview only: never the only way to the facts or actions in it.

changelog.note: Its controls carry a data-slot: `hover-card-trigger`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #329.
First release: Radix HoverCard in the popover's look, 500 ms before opening and 300 ms before closing.

items.name: tooltip

Escape inside a native <dialog> closes the dialog (a cancel it can refuse), instead of being taken by the tooltip alone.
8 px from its anchor, like the popover.
Appears and disappears.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown menu
items.description: Actions on an item; destructive actions last.

New DropdownMenuRadioGroup and DropdownMenuRadioItem: one of several in a menu, with a check beside the chosen item.
Opens the way it was opened: no keyboard ring after a click until a key moves in it.

Appears and disappears.

changelog.note: Its controls carry a data-slot: `context-menu-trigger`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #329.

First release: Radix ContextMenu in the dropdown menu's look (items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators, shortcuts, submenus; keyboard ring only in keyboard use). Long press opens it on touch.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: Search and run from the keyboard: a filterable list, and the ⌘K palette that opens over any page.

changelog.note: CommandEmpty takes a function of the query, so the no-match line can say what was typed; CommandSeparator hides while a query filters the list, so no line is left under nothing.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: CommandDialog takes `labels` (`title`, `description`); the props of the same names still work and win.
The highlighted row's ring appears only after keyboard use: at rest (a static list) there is none; it was a regression in 0.17.2.

A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules. With the keyboard, the selected row shows a 2 px inset ring. CommandDialog gives focus back to what had it before it opened (button or ⌘K); it fell to the page. An inline Command no longer scrolls the page to itself as it mounts: cmdk keeps the highlighted row in view with scrollIntoView, which also moved the page; rows now scroll their own list only.
No focus ring on the search row inside a picker popover either: the box always has focus there.
In CommandDialog the input row has no focus ring: the box always has focus there, so the ring only framed the top of the palette. On a page it still shows.
The selected item changes colour instead of jumping. The input row shows keyboard focus; new `CommandCheck` marks picked rows with a check that fades in and out.

Items use radius 8, so they sit concentric inside the 16 px panel with its 8 px padding. Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
CommandEmpty is a disabled option, so a list with no matches is never an empty listbox; it also holds a loading line.
Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
First release. The separator inside the list is decorative, so the listbox holds only groups and options.

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.description: A row of content: media, title and description, and trailing actions. Links draw the hover fill.

changelog.note: New.

items.name: icon-tile
items.title: Icon tile
items.description: A square or round surface behind one icon, in five surfaces and four sizes, with an optional status dot.

changelog.note: `variant="raised"` drops its overlay shadow: a tile is a surface, and surfaces carry none.
IconTileDot defaults to neutral (it was green).

tone="info" is neutral, like success: a tile stays on screen, and blue is only for a process someone is waiting on. Solid warning takes the mode's ink, 4.5:1 or more in every theme (it was 2.2:1 in light high contrast; solid info was 2.5:1 in dark).
tone="success" is neutral on soft and solid tiles, and its status dot is the foreground colour.
New.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A keyboard key in shortcuts and instructions; KbdGroup for chords.

changelog.note: In a tooltip the key cap and its edge take the tooltip's text colour (`primary-foreground` at 15 % and 20 %) instead of white, so they show in dark, where the tooltip is near-white (1.0:1 before, now 1.4:1 and 1.6:1; the key itself 13.7:1). Issue #301.
New `useModKey()` gives ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere. The file now starts with "use client".
`pressed` shows a key going down while its shortcut runs (it sinks and its edge thickens to the text colour, --motion-fast); useHotkeys returns which key that is.
Radius 4 (radius-2xs), so a key inside a tooltip or an input keeps clear of the corner around it.
New.

New.

items.title: Button group

Each edge fades only while content is hidden past it (the start faded at scroll 0).
The viewport shows keyboard focus again.
New.

New.

Descriptions avoid a one-word last line.
Its status pill's glyph reads the tone through `toStatus`.
New.

Issues #304, #305.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`more`, `less`; `moreLabel` and `lessLabel` still work and win). `locale` formats the counts.
Chips show keyboard focus again, and chips revealed by "N more" appear, and fade out when folded.
New.

items.name: share-bar
items.title: Share bar
items.description: How a whole splits, as one thin bar in the chart palette (the accent, two greys, Other): light enough for a table cell, with an optional label, total and legend, whose entries link to each part with href.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `share-bar-link`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
`href` on a segment makes its legend entry a link through `linkAs` (default "a"), named with its share ("Source A 4,200, 42 %"); the bar stays one picture. Without `href`, no change. Issue #296.

`locale` formats the numbers and shares.

Tracks and quiet shapes use the new --track token, so they read in dark mode (1.5:1 on their surface; they were near invisible).
New.

No unused React import, so the file compiles in projects with noUnusedLocals.
`locale` formats the numbers; `LoadMoreLabels` and `defaultLoadMoreLabels` are exported, and the label functions receive the locale.
The docs say to give newly loaded rows `animate-appear`.
New.

A revealed preview fades in.

items.name: image-grid

Pick one (`selection="single"`) is a radio group: `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`, one Tab stop, the arrow keys, Home and End move and pick, a round mark instead of a box, and picking the picked tile again keeps it.
The lightbox keeps the last picture in state set during render instead of a ref written during render, so it is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
File names stay whole when a tile is cropped; an unchecked box is an outline; the zoom button is smaller on small tiles.

First release: a gallery of thumbnails as a grid or a scroll-snap strip. Tiles keep their aspect box and load lazily; skeleton tiles while loading, hidden pictures through RestrictedPreview, a broken picture shows its file name. Single or multiple picking (aria-pressed, a ring in the focus ink and a check). A lightbox on Dialog with the position (3 of 24), ← → to move, Esc to close, focus back on the tile.

items.name: annotated-image
items.title: Annotated image
items.description: Boxes, points, polygons and poses over a picture, in its own pixel space: predicted solid, ground truth dashed, the previous version dotted, each on a halo; class words, a line-style legend, selection by keyboard, raster overlays, loading and failed states.

For grounded-text.

First release: AnnotatedImage (src or image, width, height, annotations of box, point, polygon and keypoints) with an SVG in the picture's pixel space and non-scaling strokes; predicted solid, ground truth dashed, previous dotted and faded, each on a halo; selected 3 px with handles; class words (all, selected or none); a role=img summary, or with onSelectedChange one Tab stop, arrows, Enter and Esc; overlays; loading and failed states; and AnnotationLegend for the kinds present.

items.name: grounded-text
