changelog.note: First release.

items.name: media-player
items.title: Media player
items.description: A recorded clip (a robot's camera recording, an incident clip) with the kit's controls over a native video: play, a timeline with event markers, time, mute, speed, captions and full screen on a scrim; keys while focused; loading, buffering and unavailable states.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `media-player-marker`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
Uses the theme's `bg-scrim` and `bg-letterbox` (needs `syncrobotic-theme` 0.31.0); looks the same. Issue #302.

Opens at `startAt` on a server-rendered page too (the picture stayed at 0:00 under a time reading 0:40). The Clip unavailable notice sits on its own surface, so its reason reads (it was 3.2:1 over a bright frame). Marker ticks on the timeline are 24 × 24 targets (they were 24 × 16).
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
A duration hint that arrives later is taken in the render that brings it instead of an effect later, so it is safe under the React Compiler.

First release: MediaPlayer (label, src, poster, duration, startAt, markers, tracks, loading, unavailable, onRetry, autoPlay, preload, labels) over a native <video>: play / pause, a timeline (the kit's Slider, read as "0:42 of 1:00") with marker ticks and a list of markers under the player, time in tabular numbers, mute, speed 0.5–2×, captions drawn above the controls, full screen. Space / K, ← / →, J / L, M and F while focus is in the player. Controls on a scrim in the dark theme, hidden while playing once the pointer rests, kept while a finger is on them; no autoplay under reduced motion; loading, buffering and "Clip unavailable: …" with a retry.

items.name: camera-feed
items.title: Camera feed
items.description: A robot's live camera over a native video the app feeds (a WebRTC stream or a URL): Live with the latency, Stalled with the last frame's time when frames stop, Paused while the view is frozen here, connecting, offline and no-camera states; pause view, snapshot, mute and full screen; overlays drawn over the picture.

changelog.note: `bare` shows just the picture (no header, controls, keys, Tab stop or announcement) for a feed inside something that names it and takes the keyboard, such as a camera-wall tile; `onStateChange(state, lastFrameAt)` reports each state once; `CameraFeedStateLine` and `cameraFeedStateWord` export the header's state (shape and word) so a wall's tiles say it the same way.
A new source resets the feed's state in the render that brings it instead of an effect later, and the frame callbacks' ref is updated after commit, so it is safe under the React Compiler.

First release: CameraFeed (label, source, stream or src, status, latencyMs, staleAfterMs, offlineReason, onRetry, onSnapshot, audio, aspectRatio, children, labels) over a native <video> the app feeds. The header says the camera, the robot and the state by shape and word: Live with the latency, Connecting (blue spinner), Stalled · last frame 14:02:31 over a dimmed picture after staleAfterMs without a frame (requestVideoFrameCallback, else timeupdate), Paused, Camera offline with an optional Reconnect, No camera. Pause view, snapshot (PNG), mute only with audio, full screen; Space and F while focus is inside. Overlays in a layer over the picture; aspectRatio holds the layout before the first frame. No streaming library.

items.name: camera-wall
items.title: Camera wall
items.description: Many robot cameras at once, each a camera-feed: an auto grid (1, 2×2, 3×3, 4×4 by count and width) with a page control, one camera focused large with a strip of the rest (click or Enter, Esc back, full screen), and a vertical list on phones. Tiles off screen or behind the focused one pause, only the focused camera asks the product's source function for high quality, and at most maxLive stream at once; the rest keep their last still, "Paused to save bandwidth". Each tile says its camera, robot and state (Live, Stalled · last frame 14:02:31, offline) and its robot's alarm by shape and word; sorted attention first or by name, filtered to what needs attention; arrow keys between tiles; state changes announced politely, throttled.

changelog.note: First release.

items.name: joint-state
items.title: Joint state
items.description: A robot arm's joints for monitoring (ROS sensor_msgs/JointState with the URDF's limits): each joint's position in degrees or millimetres on a thin track between its limits, velocity and effort, near-limit and at-limit in words with an icon, and loading, empty and stale states.

changelog.note: Without `locale`, numbers are written in English ("en") instead of the runtime's language, so server and browser render the same and the page hydrates without a mismatch; pass your app's locale. An invalid locale tag falls back to "en" instead of throwing. Without `updatedAt`, Stale now follows the values (position, velocity, effort), so a parent that rebuilds `joints` every render still sees Stale; a still arm then reads Stale too, so pass `updatedAt`. `staleAfterMs={Infinity}` never goes stale, an infinite URDF limit counts as no limit (no NaN marker), and ±0.05 round the same way.
First release.

items.name: diagnostics
items.title: Diagnostics
items.description: A robot's hardware and software health as ROS diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray reports it: the worst level and the counts first, then a tree by the names' "/" paths with the worst level rolled up to each group, each status as a glyph and a word that opens to its values, Stale when updates stop, a Problems filter and search by name.

changelog.note: First release. A value that is a plain number with an optional unit is grouped in `locale` (“1204553 ticks” → “1,204,553 ticks”); versions, IDs and words are shown as sent (`formatDiagnosticValue`).

items.name: point-cloud
items.title: Point cloud
items.description: A LiDAR or depth point cloud (a decoded ROS PointCloud2) drawn with raw WebGL2 and no 3D library: coloured by height or intensity on the accent's single-hue ramp with its scale, a recessive ground grid, the robot at the origin and an axes gizmo in words; orbit, pan and zoom by pointer, touch and keyboard; loading, empty, error, stale and no-WebGL states.

changelog.note: A colorRange written inline no longer re-uploads the whole cloud on every render; resizing no longer flashes an empty frame; under Windows High Contrast the points stay visible (CanvasText on Canvas); a lost pointer capture ends the drag; the middle button no longer starts autoscroll; wheels that scroll by lines or pages zoom the right amount; a live cloud reuses its buffers instead of allocating new ones for each scan. Screen readers now hear a stable name (the label and “3D point cloud”) with the count and extent in the description, which changes at most every 5 s. New label `viewName`; new exports `pointCloudWheelZoom` and `pointCloudPaletteSources`; `packPointCloud` takes an optional array to pack into.
First release.

items.name: robot-model
items.title: Robot model
items.description: A robot's pose in 3D from its URDF and live joint values (ROS sensor_msgs/JointState), for monitoring: neutral greys from the theme, a ground grid and axes named in words; highlighted joints in a status colour with a callout naming them; orbit, pan and zoom by pointer and keys; loading, error with the failing file, empty, stale and no-WebGL states in words. The kit's one three.js item.

changelog.note: Stale is said once, in the header's state line, not again over the view (the dimmed pose stays).

Mimic joints follow the joint they mimic with limits ignored on every joint, and the driving joint's value wins over a mimic's own whatever the order; a mimic joint can be highlighted by name (`RobotModelInfo.mimics`). Planar and floating joints take [x, y, θ] and [x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw] and are written per component in mm and ° (new `poseValue` label, `jointValueWords`, `jointValueOf`); one number no longer leaves their other components undefined.

Stale now follows the joint values (or `updatedAt`), not the `joints` object: an inline record no longer keeps the view fresh, or flips it in and out of Stale and announces it on every render; without `updatedAt` a robot holding still goes stale. A view rebuilt after a lost context no longer stays on “Restoring the 3D view…”, and a context not back within 5 s shows an error with Load again (new label `contextFailed`). An empty URDF file is an error instead of an endless load; meshes that arrive after the view is gone are freed; mesh paths with a query string load; a theme set on any ancestor is followed; a theme colour that does not parse no longer takes the previous one.
First release.

items.name: filter-form
items.title: Filter form
items.description: Filters kept in the URL: a GET form that applies itself after typing stops or at once on a pick, resets the page, and works without JavaScript.

changelog.note: New.

items.name: filters
items.title: Filters
items.description: A query people build from chips: + Filter picks a field, an operator and a value; each rule is a chip whose parts reopen that step. Rules combine with AND, live in the URL and filter rows in the browser.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `filters-field`, `filters-operator`, `filters-value`, `filters-remove`, `filters-back`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
The bar can shrink in a toolbar row (min-w-0): on a phone a long rule's value truncates and its remove button stays on screen.
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
The chip parts' click handlers are written on each button instead of being built in render, so the bar is safe under the React Compiler. No visible change.
`locale` formats the options' counts.
+ Filter and Clear all stay together on one line.
With several values, the first name truncates and the +N count always stays visible.

With the picker open, another part of the same chip switches it to that step in place (it closed, and a second click was needed); the part already open closes it. Fields without an icon keep the icon's space, so names line up.

First release: a flat filter bar. + Filter opens a picker (field, operator, value) built on Command in a Popover; rules are chips whose parts reopen their step; AND between chips; text, option (single or multi), number (with unit), date and boolean fields; toSearchParams / toQueryString / fromSearchParams for the URL and filterRows / matchRule for rows in the browser.

items.name: search-field
items.title: Search field
items.description: The tool's one search box: / focuses it, Enter opens the results page, and on that page it follows ?q= and applies as you type.

changelog.note: `onValueChange` (with `value`, optional) filters what is already on the screen instead of navigating: called as you type, and Enter does nothing more.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`label`, `placeholder`); the props of the same names still work and win.
New.

items.name: theme-toggle
items.title: Theme toggle
items.description: Light, match the system, or dark: three icon segments, the current one inverted, each named for screen readers.

changelog.note: Its controls carry a data-slot: `theme-toggle`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #329.
`variant="menu"`: one icon button showing the choice, which opens Light, Match system and Dark as a menu.
value is optional: leave it out until the stored choice is known (the type said it was required).
No unused React import, so the file compiles in projects with noUnusedLocals.
New.

items.name: route-progress
items.title: Route progress
items.description: A thin blue bar while the next page loads: shows after 300 ms, never reaches the end, gives up after 10 s.

changelog.note: When the page is in, the bar grows from where it got to and then fades, instead of jumping to the full width. Under reduced motion it shows the whole width at once rather than a fixed 60 % that read as real progress. It sits below the safe area (notch, status bar) when the page runs full screen.
When the page is in, the bar fills the width and fades instead of vanishing mid-way.
The bar leaves in the same render `active` turns false instead of an effect later, so it is safe under the React Compiler.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels.loading`; `label` still works and wins.
New.

items.name: autocomplete
items.title: Autocomplete
items.description: A text field that suggests as you type: filter, arrows, Enter, groups, server search with loading.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `autocomplete-input`, `autocomplete-clear`, `autocomplete-trigger`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
A new selection writes its label into the field in the render that brings it instead of an effect later, so it is safe under the React Compiler.

Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`AutocompleteLabels`: placeholder, empty, searching, searchingStatus, clear, showAll, suggestions). `placeholder` and `emptyText` still work and win over it.
Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface).

A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules. With the keyboard, the active suggestion shows a 2 px inset ring; the suggestions panel has a name.

The chevron turns while the list is open; the clear button fades in and out with the query; the highlight moves with a colour change; the selected check fades in. `debounce` (ms) sends `onQueryChange` when the typing pauses, through useDebouncedCallback; clearing never waits.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: A one-time code or PIN, one 44 px box per character, with paste and SMS autofill.

changelog.note: A full code no longer changes when you keep typing: input-otp kept the last character selected, so each key swapped the last box. Backspace, select-all and paste still edit. On a phone a long code's boxes give a few px each instead of overflowing.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: phone-input
items.title: Phone input
items.description: A phone number with its country, formatted as you type, stored as E.164.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `phone-input-number`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
Inside a Field the number box is named by the Field's label ("On-call phone"), as documented; it was always "Phone number". Alone it is still "Phone number".
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`country`, `phoneNumber`). `locale` names and sorts the countries in that language (English when left out, as before).

Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface). Read-only and disabled draw one continuous outline (the country segment had none).
A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules.
The country list takes its own width from the trigger's left edge instead of the trigger's 128 px, so names are no longer cut; a long name ends in an ellipsis and the code keeps its column.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: A month grid for one day, several days or a range; 36 px days with a mouse, 44 px on touch.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `calendar-day`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

Runs on react-day-picker 10: run npm i react-day-picker@^10 with the update; it looks and behaves the same. Props removed in v10 no longer type-check: fromMonth/fromYear and toMonth/toYear become startMonth and endMonth, fromDate/toDate become startMonth/endMonth plus hidden={{ before }} / {{ after }}, initialFocus becomes autoFocus, onDayKeyUp/onDayPointer*/onDayTouch* are gone, and old classNames keys (day_selected, caption, head_cell…) take their v9 names (selected, month_caption, weekday…). Persian, Hijri and other non-Gregorian calendars moved to @daypicker/* packages.
With a react-day-picker `locale` that names its days (`zhTW` from react-day-picker/locale), the day buttons use that locale's words instead of the kit's English ones.
With two or more months, days of neighbouring months are hidden (an end day showed twice) and months wrap when narrow.
Month and year menus are a full compact-control target (44 px on touch, 48 in gloves). Previous and next sit on the caption row (they were 12 px above it).
Month and year dropdowns show keyboard focus and a down chevron inline with the label; week numbers use a narrow column so the month fits a phone.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: date-selector
items.title: Date selector
items.description: DatePicker and DateRangePicker: a field that opens a calendar, with presets and clear.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `date-selector-clear`, `date-selector-preset`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

New `today` prop: the day the calendar marks as today, so presets built from the app's today agree with it. DateRangePicker shows one month below 640 px, so the popover fits a phone; two (numberOfMonths) from there up.

Runs on react-day-picker 10: update it together with @syncrobotic/calendar and run npm i react-day-picker@^10; its props, look and keyboard are unchanged. Import calendarLocale per language, as v10 documents it: import { zhTW } from "react-day-picker/locale/zh-TW" (react-day-picker/locale still exports it).

Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`pickDay`, `pickRange`, `clear`, `presets`). `locale` writes the trigger's day with Intl ("2026年11月3日") unless `displayFormat` is given; `calendarLocale` takes a react-day-picker locale for the calendar. Without them nothing changes.
Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface).
Its popover is named by the field, and on a small phone the calendar scrolls inside it instead of running off the screen.
The Clear button fades in and out instead of popping, and is hidden while the field is disabled.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: time-picker
items.title: Time picker
items.description: TimePicker (slots in a popover) and TimeInput (typed), on a 24-hour "HH:mm" value.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `time-picker-input`, `time-picker-option`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

A value that is not a time ("9", "9:", "25:99", "") reads as no value: the placeholder shows and no slot is picked, instead of a broken time on the trigger. An unpadded "9:30" picks the "09:30" slot; a malformed min, max or step falls back to its default. New `normalizeTime`.
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
TimeInput rewrites its text for a new value or clock in the render that brings it instead of an effect later, so it is safe under the React Compiler.

TimePicker takes `labels` (`placeholder`, `times`) and `locale`, which writes the times with Intl ("上午9:30"). `formatTime` takes an optional locale. TimeInput is unchanged: it must read back what it shows.
Disabled: the field keeps its grey fill with a --border edge, so in dark mode it no longer looks enabled; its words use the new --disabled (3:1 on every surface).

A comment says where keyboard focus shows instead of the removed outline (no change in behaviour); checked by lint:rules. The time list is one Tab stop: arrow keys, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown move, Enter or Space picks; the keyboard position shows a 2 px ring (it was a pale fill, 1.24:1, and 48 Tab stops). Its popover is named by the field.
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: data-grid
items.title: Data grid
items.description: A TanStack Table grid: sorting, pagination, selection, column menus, pinning, resizing, expandable rows, totals, loading, virtual rows.

changelog.note: DataGridColumnVisibility is --h-md, the height of the search field it sits beside in a toolbar (was --h-sm). Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `data-grid-expand`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

Column edges are focusable separators (← → resize 16 px, Shift 64 px, Home to the minimum, Enter resets) with a 24 px hit area, 44 px on touch, and the column menu offers Wider, Narrower and Reset width. Pinned columns draw their edge, the scroll fade starts after them, and pinning holds from 448 px wide only. Selected rows carry the ink bar on their first cell, pinned cells included. `selectColumn({ reason })` says why a row cannot be selected, on a grey box. New labels: width, wider, narrower, resetWidth, cannotSelect.
Needs @tanstack/react-table 9: build the table with useTable and dataGridFeatures; pinning is start/end. Keep the file's "use no memo". Looks the same.
A column's resize handle is named after the column ("Resize Robot", from meta.label or a plain-text header) instead of reading out the header function's source. Nothing to change in your code.
Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, as strict products build it; behaviour unchanged.
The selection summary keeps its count while leaving in state set during render instead of a ref, and the table notes why the compiler skips it (TanStack Virtual). No visible change.

Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: DataGrid takes `labels` (`DataGridLabels`) for every part: the region, empty text, resize handles, the header menu, the column menu, the selection summary, `selectColumn` and `expandColumn`. DataGridPagination passes `labels` to Pagination.
The same scroll cue as Table (a mask), with the edge and focus ring on the frame.

Tracks and quiet shapes use the new --track token, so they read in dark mode (1.5:1 on their surface; they were near invisible). Totals switch to the one-row summary whenever the grid scrolls sideways.
The same scroll fade as Table; the sort arrow always follows the label.
The empty state stays in view on phones, totals become one readable row on phones, and the sort arrow swaps with a fade.
`size="sm"` replaces `density="dense"`, so it is not confused with the theme's data-density. `density` still works until 1.0.
Virtual rows read their height from the token, so they follow `data-density`.
New.

items.name: log-viewer
items.title: Log viewer
items.description: Robot and system logs (ROS /rosout, journald, a service's lines): a virtual list that stays smooth with 100,000 lines, follows the newest line until someone scrolls up ("12 new · Jump to latest"), keeps the last maxLines in a ring buffer, filters by level and source, searches with the matches marked and next/previous, wraps long lines, shows clock time or time ago, opens a line for its whole message and fields, and copies a line or a selection. Levels by shape and word; lines from props or an imperative append that batches a fast stream.

changelog.note: The toolbar is one control height, the search field's --h-md: the level and source menus are default-size buttons and the view options an icon button, no longer 36 px beside a 44 px field. An opened line's detail is a band of its row instead of a ringed card under the message: a hairline, then the fields with names under the time column and values under the level column (the message cell spans the columns on a CSS subgrid), and one quiet ghost Copy line on the band. The footer's Copy shows only for a selection of two or more lines ("Copy 3 lines"). Jump to latest is docked in the footer beside Paused instead of floating over the lines.
First release. The list is a treegrid (each line opens), so screen readers accept its rows' aria-expanded.

items.name: streaming-text
items.title: Streaming text
items.description: A model's answer as it streams in, token by token. The text grows in place under a calm status row: the queue position, Generating with Stop, then "Done in 2.4 s · first token 0.3 s", Stopped or Failed with the partial answer kept. A reasoning part stays apart, closed, and screen readers hear whole sentences, never every token.

changelog.note: First release.

items.name: sortable
items.title: Sortable
items.description: A list or grid people reorder by dragging a handle, by touch or by keyboard, with announcements (dnd-kit).

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `sortable-handle`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.

Picking an item up announces only the pick-up, not a move to the place it is already in. New SortablePosition writes an item's place and follows a drag as it goes. A focused handle at the edge of a scrolling list is scrolled in with room for its focus ring.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`SortableLabels`): every drag announcement and the keyboard instructions.

The drag overlay renders on <body>, so it stays under the pointer and drops back to the right place inside a transformed container (an entrance animation, a sheet). Without `renderOverlay` the item itself follows the pointer, lifted, instead of fading and staying put.
The handle uses radius 4 (radius-2xs) inside its row.
New.

items.name: resizable
items.title: Resizable
items.description: Panels resized by dragging the line between them or with the arrow keys, horizontal, vertical or nested (react-resizable-panels).

changelog.note: The grip is visible: --input with a card ring, and it no longer collapses to 1 px.
On a touch screen the handle's hit area is 44 px wide (48 in gloves).
New.

items.name: file-upload
items.title: File upload
items.description: A drop zone that is also a button: checks type, size and count, and says what it refused.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `file-upload-input`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
With multiple off, extra files are refused as "count" through onReject instead of dropped silently; other attributes such as aria-label reach the drop zone (an icon-only zone has a name).
Disabled keeps its words readable: a grey field (bg-muted, muted text) on controls with a surface, solid disabled ink on items and icons; no more 50 % opacity, which washes text out in sunlight.
New.

items.name: attachment
items.title: Attachment
items.description: One file in a list, a composer or a queue: type, name, size, progress, error with Retry, Download and Remove.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `attachment-action`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
A long file name is cut in the middle, so its extension always shows; the whole name is in the title.
Removes a stale lint comment for a rule this kit does not use. No visible change.
Every word it says can be translated without editing the source: `labels` (`AttachmentLabels`: "Upload failed", "Failed", the percentage, and the Retry, Download, Cancel, Remove and progress names).
New.

items.name: file-type
items.title: File type
items.description: An icon for a file from its name or extension, with robot formats (mcap, bag, pgm, pcd, onnx) and the extension written on it.

changelog.note: New.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: Where someone is in a fixed sequence of steps: done, current, upcoming and error steps, horizontal or vertical, with a compact bar for phones.

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `stepper-step`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
On a narrow stepper, a failed step's title and reason show under the row, so the cross is never shown without its reason.

Steps share the row equally. When there is not about 6rem per step, the labels go to screen readers and the current step's title and description show once, full width, under the row (they were squeezed into their share and hyphenated).
Horizontal steps are equal width with labels centred under their dots and connectors from dot to dot; a narrow stepper keeps only the current step's label; step buttons show keyboard focus again.

New.

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline

A warning or danger event says so to screen readers (", warning", ", failed"), as Marker does; the glyph alone was visual only.
A horizontal timeline fades its last visible event when more are hidden (now a client component).
The horizontal timeline shows keyboard focus again.

New.

items.name: scrollspy
items.title: Scrollspy

changelog.note: Every button, link and field it draws carries a data-slot: `scrollspy-link`, so a product's check for hand-made controls can tell them from its own. Issue #317.
On a page or panel with nothing to scroll, the first section is current at load, not the last.
Links show keyboard focus again.
Chips use radius 8.
New.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation menu

New.

items.name: questionnaire
items.title: Questionnaire
items.description: A short set of questions, one per page or all on one form: single and multiple choice, scales and text, required checks and a review page.

A paged form with no questions renders and Next does nothing, instead of throwing. Compiles with noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

New.

items.name: marker
items.title: Marker
items.description: A labelled line across a log or feed (a day, a takeover, an e-stop), and MarkerRow: one dense log line with a status glyph, detail and time.

Its glyph reads the tone through `toStatus`.
New.

items.name: stats-cards

Icon to label 8 px (gap-2), the same in every component.
Sparklines neutral; only a change for the worse is coloured.

items.name: fleet-table
items.title: Fleet table

Search is an InputGroup.
First versioned release. Earlier history is in CHANGELOG.md.

items.title: Robot status card

changelog.note: The design language says a toolbar is one height (every control --h-md beside a field, --h-sm only in a row without one) and where the app shell's collapse controls sit. The checklist says a status page inside top-bar-shell takes `as="h1"` and links out with `{ label, href }`. Issue #323. Design language: `bg-scrim`, `bg-letterbox` and the chart inks (`text-chart-N-foreground`). Design language: `--shell-top` and `--shell-surface`, set by every shell, for pinning a tab row (TabsList sticky) or a filter bar under the top bar. Skill: the data blocks' `…Content` exports, to use inside a product's own frame instead of a second shell. The checklist names StreamingText for a model's streamed answer. Design language: marks linked to something outside the picture (a hovered word, a row) are highlighted in the selected ink at 3 px, keeping their line style, and the rest fade (grounded-text); never a colour per link. Radius: `rounded-[inherit]` is allowed on a child that fills its parent edge to edge (a scroll viewport, an avatar's picture, a stretched link's hit area), so a product lint that enforces the scale can allow it by rule. Issue #301. Checklist: CardTitle, AccordionTrigger and PageHeader take `as`, CardDataHeader `titleAs`, so headings skip no level. Issue #303.
Design language and checklist: the chart palette is graphite and one accent (the brand indigo), series told apart by line style too, three series and Other at most, heatmaps on the accent's ramp.
Design language: --track for tracks and quiet shapes.

The design language and checklist carry the rules settled in 0.17: offline is calm grey; battery is a Meter that warns below 15 % and never turns danger; a switch on is primary; a KPI change is coloured only when worse; the environment badge is neutral; field edges use --input at 3:1; outlined buttons stay outlined when disabled; an overview puts alarms first; every chart has a table view; focus rings are never removed. The design language and checklist match the foundations word for word: 44 px on touch and 36 with a mouse; disabled outlines; elevation recipes with ring-1; six motion patterns; exit easing via the exit animations; waiting loops; a table view for every chart with axes; IconTile and Progress success are neutral; weights; WCAG large text.

Design language: annotations on images (line style first, a halo under every stroke, class as a word not a colour) and the action rail (only the next step; ← and Esc go back). Test and audit results: a pass is grey with a check, a failure a danger outline, not enough samples grey with a dashed circle.
Design language: disabled text is `text-disabled` on text-only controls, 3:1 and lighter than secondary text; say why something is disabled.
Design language: page transitions move only the content; the root and the stop are never in a view transition, which blocks clicks while it runs.
Design language: high contrast, how many chart series (five in lines and bars, three in scatter and maps), floating sheets and top bars.
Light is the default theme; dark is for control rooms and night shifts.

Links point to design-system.syncrobotic.me. The design language and checklist catch up with 0.10 and 0.11: blue only for a process being waited on, calm states grey, readable disabled text, the exit easing, the 2xs radius and the type scale, density, touch and sound, the icon set and the alarm states.
First release.
